To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Maternal HIV-1 viral load in DNA form is an independent predictor of MTCT of HIV-1.

HIV-1 DNA-viral load was associated with mother-to-child transmission in a population of pregnant HIV-infected women who received antenatal zidovudin prophylaxis and whose infants received neonatal zidovulin, and that HIV-1 RNA-viral load was not associated with mother-to-children transmission.
Maternal HIV DNA load is associated with MTCT independently from RNA-VL.

maternal HIV-1 DNA and mother-to-child HIV transmission.

the role of cell-associated HIV- DNA in MTCT in a cohort of women who received prophylaxis during their pregnancies and whose infants received prophylaxis after birth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA-VL is a better indicator of the MTCT of HIV-1 than is the RNA-VL, but that both RNA-VL and DNA-VL are better indicators of the MTCT than is the CD4 count.

the DNA viral load is associated with the risk of MTCT of HIV-1 in a population of HIV-1 infected women who received antiviral prophylaxis and that this association is independent of the RNA viral load.

maternal HIV-1 DNA VL was associated with MTCS in a population of HIV-1-infected pregnant women who received antepartum antiretrovirus prophylaxis and whose infants were administered zidovudin after birth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIV DNA viral load is an independent risk factor for mother-to-child transmission in women receiving zidovudin prophylaxis during their pregnancy.
maternal DNA viral load is an important factor in predicting MTCT of HIV-1 in women who receive antiretrovirals during pregnancy.

HIV-1 DNA is a better indicator of MTCT than HIV-1 RNA, especially when antiretrovirals are used to prevent transmission, and therefore, HIV-1 RNA should be used to monitor antiretrovial therapy in pregnant women.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maternal HIV-1 DNA VL was associated with MTTC in a population of Thai women who received zido-vudine prophylax-is during pregnancy and whose children received zidov-u-dine after birth.
HIV-1 DNA VL is a better predictor of mother-to-child transmission than RNA VL.
DNA-VL is a strong predictor of MTCT, and that it should be considered as a complementary tool to RNA-VL for the management and prevention of MTCT of HIV.
